content.text: I read the release and the brief line by line and checked each figure, period and basis.

facts.evidence: Consolidated revenues for the second quarter totaled $31.6 billion, an increase of 2.3% from the year-ago quarter, driven by growth in Advanced Connectivity fiber and wireless revenues.
Diluted earnings per share from continuing operations were $0.66, compared to $0.62 in the prior year period
adjusted diluted EPS was $0.65, versus $0.54 in the year-ago quarter
Advanced Connectivity service revenue grew 5.1% year over year to $23.5 billion
Adjusted EBITDA reached $12.3 billion, representing a 5.2% increase year over year
The company reiterates its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $2.25 to $2.35 and expects free cash flow of $18 billion or more for the year.
AT&T plans to return approximately $45 billion to shareholders during 2026-2028 through dividends and share repurchases, including accelerating share repurchases to approximately $10 billion in 2026.
with free cash flow of $4.7 billion compared to $4.4 billion in the prior year period
Legacy segment revenues declined 25.9% to $1.6 billion as the company continues decommissioning its copper-based network
a record quarter for combined fiber and fixed wireless net adds totaling 646,000 ... including 432,000 postpaid phone net adds with a churn rate of 0.86%

claims.claim: Consolidated revenues for the second quarter totaled $31.6 billion.
Second-quarter revenues increased 2.3% from the year-ago quarter.
The revenue increase was driven by growth in Advanced Connectivity fiber and wireless revenues.
Diluted EPS from continuing operations was $0.66, compared with $0.62 in the year-ago quarter.
Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.65, versus $0.54 in the year-ago quarter.
Operating income was $7.0 billion.
Adjusted operating income was $7.5 billion.
Both operating income and adjusted operating income were up from $6.5 billion in the second quarter of 2025.
Adjusted EBITDA was $12.3 billion.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 5.2% year over year.
Free cash flow was $4.7 billion, compared with $4.4 billion in the year-ago quarter.
Advanced Connectivity service revenue grew 5.1% year over year to $23.5 billion.
The quarter was a record for combined fiber and fixed wireless net adds, totaling 646,000.
The company added more than 1 million Advanced Connectivity customers.
Postpaid phone net adds were 432,000.
Postpaid phone churn was 0.86%.
Total fiber locations reached 38.6 million.
Legacy segment revenues declined 25.9% to $1.6 billion.
The Legacy revenue decline reflects continued decommissioning of the copper-based network.
Legacy segment operating expenses decreased 10.8% year over year.
The company reiterates full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $2.25 to $2.35.
The company expects free cash flow of $18 billion or more for 2026.
Management maintains its long-term outlook for service revenue growth in the low-single-digit range annually through 2028.
Advanced Connectivity service revenue is expected to grow in the mid-single-digit range.
AT&T plans to return approximately $45 billion to shareholders during 2026-2028 through dividends and share repurchases.
claims.note: The release states plans to return "$45 billion+" over 2026-2028, i.e., a floor; the brief converts that minimum into an approximate amount, which understates the commitment as disclosed.

claims.claim: Share repurchases are being accelerated to approximately $10 billion in 2026.
Total debt was $144.0 billion at the end of the second quarter.
Net debt was $126.4 billion after accounting for cash and time deposits.
Capital investment totaled $6.1 billion in the quarter.
Capital expenditures related to continuing operations were $5.7 billion in the quarter.
The company plans to maintain annual capital investment in the $23 billion to $24 billion range through 2028.
The company returned $4.1 billion to shareholders during the quarter.
Approximately $2.2 billion of that was common share repurchases under its existing authorization.
The release states legacy EBITDA is expected to turn negative after 2027 until AT&T substantially eliminates direct costs associated with operating its copper-based network.
Obtaining approvals for decommissioning could affect the timeline.
Operating expenses increased due to an asset abandonment charge related to spectrum strategy reprioritization and higher bad debt expenses driven by subscriber growth.
